before: in all other manifestations.
after: in all manifestations.
reason: The word other removed. This phase of perfection exists in only one manifestation—relative perfection.

before: all of infinite Deity potentials
after: all infinite Deity potentials
reason: The 1955 construction is awkward because all of is used to modify potentials without the latter being qualified by a limiting adjective.

before: relatively quiet zone
after: relatively quiet zones
reason: The plural agrees with the verb are.

before: of outer space in the realms
after: of outer space, in the realms
reason: The comma is required to set off the parenthetical phrase.

before: Tertiary circuit supervisor No. 572,842
after: Tertiary circuit supervisor number 572,842
reason: The spelled-out version is appropriate in this context.

before: The Significance of Origins are
after: The Significances of Origins are
reason: The plural is required to agree with the verb are.

before: the Significance of Origins teach
after: the Significances of Origins teach
reason: The plural is required to agree with the verb are.

before: the Seven Central Supervisors
after: the Seven Center Supervisors
reason: There is no other reference to Seven Central Supervisors, but there are multiple references to Seven Center Supervisors who function closely with the Supreme Power Directors.

before: beings enroute elsewhere who pause
after: beings en route elsewhere who pause
reason: Enroute is incorrect French and is not the form that has been adopted into English.

before: subsequently add any thing new
after: subsequently add anything new
reason: The closed word is the correct choice in this case.

before: secondary Universe Circuit Supervisor
after: tertiary Universe Circuit Supervisor
reason: Only the tertiary Circuit Supervisor is stationed within the local universe.

before: Paradise Son of God the Supreme Power Centers
after: Paradise Son of God, the Supreme Power Centers
reason: The comma indicates the end of the prepositional phrase.

before: having become sixty thousand times as dense
after: having become forty thousand times as dense
reason: Textual consistency and current scientific estimates of our sun’s density both support forty thousand.

before: the Y rays of radium
after: the gamma rays of radium
reason: Y rays written out as gamma rays.

before: an electron weighs a little less than
after: an electron weighs a little more than
reason: More is consistent with 42:6.8, where the author states that a proton is eighteen hundred times as heavy as an electron, and is also in general agreement with current scientific opinion which places the ratio at about 1:1836.

before: weighs from two to three thousand times more
after: weighs almost two thousand times more
reason: The calculation of the relative masses of the electron and the hydrogen atom was undergoing a rapid evolution just prior to the writing of The Urantia Book, the ratio being 1:1700 in 1897; 1:2000 in 1904; and 1:1845 by 1922. This last ratio is also the one quoted in the 1934 Webster’s Dictionary.

before: relative cosmic reality from the
after: relative cosmic reality, from the
reason: The comma correctly separates the following parenthetical phrase.

before: established almost four thousand years ago
after: established almost forty thousand years ago
reason: The announcement was made shortly after the default of Adam and Eve which occurred about 37,800 years ago.

before: you are rekeyed each time
after: you are re-keyed each time
reason: The only other occurrence of re-keyed is in hyphenated form at 48:2.21.

before: universe headquarters worlds, may be found
after: universe headquarters worlds may be found
reason: Although technically acceptable, the comma makes the sentence more difficult to read.

before: Some time they hope to be granted
after: Sometime they hope to be granted
reason: The closed form is correct as the reference is to an indefinite point in time rather than to an indefinite period of time.

before: spheres of the universe, the superuniverse, and of Havona
after: spheres of the universe, the superuniverse, and Havona
reason: Parallel structure established by removing the word of.

before: In your world, even in the face of
after: On your world, even in the face of
reason: This does not appear to be a valid use of in.

before: Of the 681,227 Material Sons lost in Satania
after: Of the 681,217 Material Sons lost in Satania
reason: The correction from 681,227 to 681,217 was made because of the original’s conflict with 51:1.5.

before: the ministering-spirit quartette, becomes attached to
after: the ministering-spirit quartet, becomes attached to
reason: Quartette and quartet each occur once in The Urantia Book. There is no differentiation in meaning between the two spellings, so the text has been standardized to quartet to facilitate electronic searching.

before: The ministering-spirit quartettes consist of
after: The ministering-spirit quartets consist of
reason: Quartettes and quartets each occur once in The Urantia Book. There is no differentiation in meaning between the two spellings, so the text has been standardized to quartets to facilitate electronic searching.

before: On the worlds the Trinity Teacher Sons
after: On these worlds the Trinity Teacher Sons
reason: The demonstrative adjective these distinguishes which worlds are being discussed.

before: on the other hand the new orders of beings
after: on the other hand, the new orders of beings
reason: The structure of the sentence calls for a comma.

before: 900,000,000,000 years ago the Uversa archives testify
after: 900,000,000,000 years ago, the Uversa archives testify
reason: The comma properly encloses the descriptive phrase.

before: life has a marine origin the ideal conditions
after: life has a marine origin, the ideal conditions
reason: The comma is required.

before: about one two-billionths
after: about one two-billionth
reason: The singular is correct.

before: Ameba are typical survivors
after: Amebas are typical survivors
reason: The plural is required here to agree with are.

before: a veritable tropic Paradise paradise
after: a veritable tropic paradise
reason: Paradise should be lower case.

before: the muscles mussels, clams, oysters, and scallops
after: the mussels, clams, oysters, and scallops
reason: Muscles is now so uncommon for this meaning that the modern form has been adopted.

before: marine-life evolution, the age of fishes
after: marine-life evolution, the age of fishes
reason: The article the removed from italics.

before: 85,000,000 years ago Bering Strait
after: 85,000,000 years ago the Bering Strait
reason: The usage was correct when The Urantia Book was written but is now so unfamiliar that the insertion is justified.

before: But some time previously there had appeared
after: But sometime previously there had appeared
reason: The closed form is correct as the reference is to an indefinite point in time rather than to an indefinite period of time.

before: the Panama Isthmus went up
after: the Panama isthmus went up
reason: Capitalization is used only for the formal name of a geographical feature.

before: three times Bering Strait land bridge
after: three times the Bering Strait land bridge
reason: The usage was correct when The Urantia Book was written but is now so unfamiliar that the insertion is justified.

before: Bering Strait land bridge was up
after: The Bering Strait land bridge was up
reason: The usage was correct when The Urantia Book was written but is now so unfamiliar that the insertion is justified.

before: Weasels, martins, otters, and raccoons thrived
after: Weasels, martens, otters, and raccoons thrived
reason: Martins is now so uncommon for this meaning that the modern form has been adopted.

before: most of the State of Iowa
after: most of the state of Iowa
reason: Capitalization removed from State.

before: the beginning of the Holocene or postglacial period
after: the beginning of the Holocene or postglacial period
reason: All other geologic periods are italicized.

before: the flint flakers and stonemasons
after: the flint flakers and stone masons
reason: The spelling has been standardized to the open form.

before: The dispensation of the Prince has passed, the age of Adam
after: The dispensation of the Prince has passed; the age of Adam
reason: The initial clause is a complete sentence; a semicolon is the correct way of linking the two parts of the larger sentence.

before: In the days of the first Eden Adam had
after: In the days of the first Eden, Adam had
reason: The comma appropriately separates the initial adverbial phrase.

before: a descendant of Nod, was indorsed.
after: a descendant of Nod, was endorsed.
reason: Indorsed is obsolete, the modern form endorsed is justified.

before: the purpose of building the tower.
after: the purpose of building the tower:
reason: This sentence clearly introduces a list, so the colon is appropriate.

before: all sorts of sick peoples
after: all sorts of sick people
reason: Peoples indicate not multiple individuals but multiple large groups of people.

before: a civilization in anyway comparable
after: a civilization in any way comparable
reason: The two-word form any way is the appropriate choice when serving as an adverb.

before: commerical civilization of the world
after: commercial civilization of the world
reason: Simply a spelling error in typesetting.

before: land passage to the west, over the Bering isthmus
after: land passage to the West, over the Bering isthmus
reason: West is referring to the Western Hemisphere, thus indicating a place rather than a direction of travel.

before: disruption of Graeco-Roman civilization
after: disruption of Greco-Roman civilization
reason: The more modern form was decided upon.

before: level of the Atlantic Ocean Presently the
after: level of the Atlantic Ocean. Presently the
reason: This period, at the end of the last line on the page in the original format, was missing in the first printing.

before: Central Europe was for sometime controlled by
after: Central Europe was for some time controlled by
reason: The two-word form is correct as the reference is to an indefinite period of time.

before: there persisted for sometime a superior civilization
after: there persisted for some time a superior civilization
reason: The two-word form is correct as the reference is to an indefinite period of time.

before: a life-long partnership of self-effacement
after: a lifelong partnership of self-effacement
reason: Standardization was decided here.

before: enhancement of parental instinct. Each generation
after: enhancement of parental instinct — each generation
reason: The correction makes this section consistent with the other three items of this series.

before: The children of Badanon developed
after: The children of Badonan developed
reason: Badonan is the correct spelling.
note: The Foundation page links this row to 84:7.7.

before: make sure that some one would provide
after: make sure that someone would provide
reason: The compound form is used when the group of which the "one" is a member is not specified.

before: grew up as a defense against evil eye
after: grew up as a defense against the evil eye
reason: The phrase evil eye without an article seems extremely stilted.

before: good luck, evil eye, and astrology
after: good luck, the evil eye, and astrology
reason: The phrase evil eye without an article seems extremely stilted.

before: the custom to forego many forms
after: the custom to forgo many forms
reason: The corrected spelling of forgo is etymologically preferable.

before: 5,740,352 sacks of coin
after: 5,740,352 sacks of corn
reason: The list of gifts to the Gods is excerpted from the Harris Papyrus I, which predates the earliest significant presence of coins in Egypt by 650-750 years.

before: dedication to life-long virginity
after: dedication to lifelong virginity
reason: Standardization was decided here.

before: the Shawnee Teuskwatawa,
after: the Shawnee Tenskwatawa,
reason: Tenskwatawa is the standard transliteration for the Shawnee prophet’s name.

before: the eclipse of the sun in 1808
after: the eclipse of the sun in 1806
reason: The date in the text has been corrected because the incident actually occurred in 1806.

before: religions of ancient times were Judaism and Hinduism, and each
after: religions of ancient times were Hinduism and Judaism, and each
reason: The correction in word order is consistent with the subsequent phraseology, “...each respectively...in Orient and Occident.” At some point it appears a transcription error was made and this is the simplest way to restore the intended meaning.

before: Level values — loyalties
after: Level of values — loyalties
reason: Level values has no discernible meaning; Level of values is meaningful, consistent with the context, and is consistent with the other three items in this series.

before: for Abraham to forego
after: for Abraham to forgo
reason: The corrected spelling of forgo is etymologically preferable.

before: such as Agni, Indra, Soma
after: such as Agni, Indra, and Soma
reason: The conjunction and between the last two elements of a series gives the reader an indication that the series is complete.

before: and in this country, far distant
after: and in this country, far-distant
reason: The decision to standardize usage is in agreement with Webster’s of 1934.

before: He taught that “man’s eternal destiny was everlasting union
after: He taught that man’s eternal destiny was “everlasting union
reason: The relocation of the opening quotation mark resolves the difficulty.

before: Such teaching gained the ascendency
after: Such teaching gained the ascendancy
reason: Ascendancy is first choice of Webster’s and is definitely preferred above ascendency.

before: in the Arabian desert
after: in the Arabian Desert
reason: The correct form is Arabian Desert.

before: to the Arabian desert
after: to the Arabian Desert
reason: The correct form is Arabian Desert.

before: But none the less he sought
after: But nonetheless he sought
reason: None the less is used when the meaning is equivalent to no less, and nonetheless is used when the meaning approximates even so.

before: walk humbly with your God.”
after: walk humbly with your God?”
reason: This quote is punctuated as found in the Revised Version Bible.

before: the ascendency of Egypt brought
after: the ascendancy of Egypt brought
reason: Ascendancy is first choice of Webster’s and is definitely preferred above ascendency.

before: more than twoscore self-elevated human deities
after: more than two-score self-elevated human deities
reason: The hyphenated form is the consistent usage elsewhere in the text. The decision was made to standardize on that form.

before: people in the Graeco-Roman world
after: people in the Greco-Roman world
reason: The more modern form was decided upon.

before: If some one irritates you
after: If someone irritates you
reason: The two-word form is appropriate when referring to some one member of a particular group.

before: Only in the second sketch you are favored
after: Only, in the second sketch you are favored
reason: The comma after Only is required to convey the intended meaning, which approximates “however."

before: adverse ani malistic tendencies
after: adverse animalistic tendencies
reason: The required hyphen at the end of the line was inserted. This issue does not occur in the electronic texts.

before: cosmic levels of the Supreme mind
after: cosmic levels of the Supreme Mind
reason: Chicago Manual of Style steadfastly recommends capitalization for names for Deity. Therefore, when using Supreme Mind as a two-word noun/name, Mind should be capitalized.

before: consciousness of true reality;
after: consciousness of true reality;
reason: Semicolon italicized.

before: Science indicates Deity as a fact;
after: Science indicates Deity as a fact;
reason: Semicolon italicized.

before: Ethics is the eternal social or racial mirror
after: Ethics is the external social or racial mirror
reason: Correcting eternal to external on the basis of an assumed keystroke error makes the sentence clear in meaning and reveals a contrastive point which is completely absent from the original.

before: corelator of the absolute and the relative
after: correlator of the absolute and the relative
reason: Correlator, the now standard form, is found five times elsewhere in the text.

before: the eternity co-existence of the Son
after: the eternity coexistence of the Son
reason: The hyphenated form is not found elsewhere in the text and is not supported.

before: and the Unrevealed Consummator of
after: and the unrevealed Consummator of
reason: The lowercase version is correct because unrevealed is solely descriptive.

before: the unknown potential of Supreme mind
after: the unknown potential of Supreme Mind
reason: Chicago Manual of Style steadfastly recommends capitalization for names for Deity.

before: Personalized Thought Adjusters are the untrammelled
after: Personalized Thought Adjusters are the untrammeled
reason: Untrammeled is the consistent usage elsewhere in the text and is preferred by Chicago Manual of Style.

before: compatible with a light-hearted and joyous life
after: compatible with a lighthearted and joyous life
reason: All other occurrences in the text follow the compound form, lighthearted.

before: the ka and the ba;
after: the ka and the ba;
reason: The semicolon should be italicized.

before: Vertical depth embraces the organismal drives
after: Vertical depth embraces the organismal drives
reason: Vertical and depth should both be italicized as together they form the substantive paralleled by the other items in the context.

before: the Jerusem corps of twenty-four planetary supervisors designate one
after: the Jerusem corps of twenty-four planetary supervisors designates one
reason: The word corps, being a collective noun, requires a singular verb form for correct noun/verb agreement.

before: while the united midwayers,
after: while the United Midwayers,
reason: United Midwayers is the usual form of the term.

before: Qualified Vicegerents of the Ultimate
after: Qualified Vicegerents of the Ultimate.
reason: This period was missing in many copies of the 1955 text but it very faintly appears in others, apparently being worn down in the course of the printing.

before: any violence to the freewillness
after: any violence to the free-willness
reason: Free-willness is found at four other locations in the text and in all instances it refers to an attribute or characteristic of a being or beings.

before: the colossal error of Pantheism
after: the colossal error of pantheism
reason: Though religions and even philosophical schools are normally capitalized, pantheism is more of a philosophical concept and is not capitalized.

before: Jesus has promised some time to return
after: Jesus has promised sometime to return
reason: The closed form of sometime is correct.

before: [This paper, depicting
after: This paper, depicting
reason: Removal of the brackets makes formatting consistent with credits at the ends of Parts I and II.
note: The 1955 text also has a closing bracket at the end of the paragraph.

before: did not hestitate to clash
after: did not hesitate to clash
reason: Simple typesetting spelling error.

before: his fifth birthday anniversay
after: his fifth birthday anniversary
reason: Simple typesetting spelling error.

before: on pleasure or business to nearby Cana
after: on pleasure or business to near-by Cana
reason: All other instances of near-by as an adjective are hyphenated.

before: to view the “gate beautiful,” the artistic gate
after: to view the “Gate Beautiful,” the artistic gate
reason: Gate Beautiful is clearly one name for this gate; therefore capitalization is appropriate.

before: he could look upon Tannach
after: he could look upon Taanach
reason: Taanach is the correct spelling and standard transliteration of the name.

before: superhuman or miraculous peformance
after: superhuman or miraculous performance
reason: Simple typesetting spelling error.

before: and the bond-servant of depression and defeat
after: and the bond servant of depression and defeat
reason: The only form found in Webster’s is the open form. Therefore, the decision was made to standardize on that form.

before: if any one should be so unthinking
after: if anyone should be so unthinking
reason: Anyone is correct if anybody could be substituted.

before: functioning of a consciousness sorter and associater
after: functioning of a consciousness sorter and associator
reason: The common form, associator, is the consistent usage elsewhere in the text.

before: religion began at 10:00 o’clock
after: religion began at ten o’clock
reason: The spelled-out form for time is clearly supported in Chicago Manual of Style.

before: sessions started at 3:00 o’clock
after: sessions started at three o’clock
reason: The spelled-out form for time is clearly supported in Chicago Manual of Style.

before: debates opened at 8:00 o’clock
after: debates opened at eight o’clock
reason: The spelled-out form for time is clearly supported in Chicago Manual of Style.

before: Sychar, Schecham
after: Sychar, Shechem
reason: Shechem is the standard transliteration of the name.

before: CaesareaPhilippi
after: Caesarea-Philippi
reason: Given the almost universal consistency of usage in the text, the hyphenated form must have been the author’s choice.

before: CaesareaPhilippi
after: Caesarea-Philippi
reason: Correction to hyphenated form.

before: took place some time before his baptism
after: took place sometime before his baptism
reason: The closed form sometime is correct as the reference is to an indefinite point in time.

before: fresh, first-hand reports
after: fresh, firsthand reports
reason: Of the five occurrences of firsthand and first-hand, only this one is hyphenated; no differentiation in usage exists.

before: bridegroom who stands near-by
after: bridegroom who stands near by
reason: Consistent adverb usage supports this correction to the open form.

before: Michael No. 611,121
after: Michael number 611,121
reason: The spelled-out version is appropriate in this context.

before: this momentous dialog of Jesus’
after: this momentous dialogue of Jesus’
reason: Though this is a more modern and American English form, it is the only instance. Multiple instances of dialogue are found.

before: their first clearcut and positive
after: their first clear-cut and positive
reason: This word is found eight additional times; all are hyphenated.

before: Judas parents were Sadducees
after: Judas’s parents were Sadducees
reason: The correct form is Judas’s.

before: He was liberal, bighearted, learned, and tolerant
after: He was liberal, big-hearted, learned, and tolerant
reason: The only other occurrence of this word is hyphenated, so it was decided to standardize on this version.

before: The Sabbath week ends they usually spent
after: The Sabbath weekends they usually spent
reason: The closed form has become the standard usage and has been adopted.

before: that I thirst not neither come all the way
after: that I thirst not, neither come all the way
reason: The comma properly separates the phrases, making this sentence easier to read.

before: preach at the week-day evening
after: preach at the weekday evening
reason: The closed form has become the standard usage and has been adopted.

before: the encouragement of evil doing
after: the encouragement of evil-doing
reason: There has been a clear preference for the hyphenated form since the seventeenth century.

before: He was a half-hearted believer
after: He was a halfhearted believer
reason: The closed form is the consistent usage elsewhere in the text. The decision was made to standardize on that form.

before: the Master among other things said, in reply
after: the Master, among other things, said in reply
reason: This required two corrections: a comma was inserted after the Master, and a pre-existing comma that followed said was moved in front.

before: return to Bethsaida some time on Thursday
after: return to Bethsaida sometime on Thursday
reason: The reference is to an indefinite point in time, therefore sometime is correct.

before: confined in one of the grottos
after: confined in one of the grottoes
reason: Though both forms are correct, this word is found elsewhere in the text as grottoes. The text was standardized on that form.

before: you are short-sighted and material-minded
after: you are shortsighted and material-minded
reason: The closed form is the consistent usage elsewhere.

before: Jairus only reply to all this
after: Jairus’s only reply to all this
reason: The correct form is Jairus’s.

before: But hearken to me all of you
after: But hearken to me, all of you
reason: The comma properly separates the phrases, making the sentence easier to read.

before: accepted the tax, foregoing the penalty for tardy payment
after: accepted the tax, forgoing the penalty for tardy payment
reason: The corrected spelling of forgoing is etymologically preferable.

before: Come out of him you unclean spirit
after: Come out of him, you unclean spirit
reason: The comma properly separates the phrases, making this sentence easier to read.

before: slept very little that night;
after: slept very little that night,
reason: The semicolon is too strong a separator. A comma is more appropriate.

before: there is deliberate evildoing and sinful rebellion
after: there is deliberate evil-doing and sinful rebellion
reason: There has been a clear preference for the hyphenated form since the seventeenth century.

before: they are at once restful and time-saving
after: they are at once restful and timesaving
reason: Though the original is clear, the closed form is the common one and was approved in Webster’s 1934.

before: He says that any one who has seen him
after: He says that anyone who has seen him
reason: The closed form is correct.

before: than this Jesus of Nazareth has already done?
after: than this Jesus of Nazareth has already done.
reason: This is an indirect question contained within a declarative sentence, so the period is correct.

before: toward the beautiful gate
after: toward the Beautiful Gate
reason: Beautiful Gate is clearly one name for this gate; therefore capitalization is appropriate.

before: who commits sin is the bondservant of sin
after: who commits sin is the bond servant of sin
reason: The only form found in Webster’s is the open form.

before: the bondservant is not likely
after: the bond servant is not likely
reason: The only form found in Webster’s is the open form.

before: during the times of Judas Maccabeus
after: during the times of Judas Maccabee
reason: Although Maccabeus is a more accurate transliteration of the Greek, Maccabee is common in English works and is used in all other occurrences in The Urantia Book.

before: set upon their own selfish gain’.”
after: set upon their own selfish gain.’”
reason: Quotation marks—single or double—should always enclose a comma or period.

before: Lord open to us
after: Lord, open to us
reason: In the original format, Lord was the last word in the line, making a dropped comma likely.

before: I must needs to go prove it
after: I must needs go to prove it
reason: The original to go is a transposition resulting in a grammatically incorrect formulation.

before: on the second, or even the third day,
after: on the second or even the third day,
reason: The form with only a comma following day is the most readable punctuation.

before: he had become enamoured
after: he had become enamored
reason: This word is also found at 121:5.6; there, the American spelling is used. The American form was adopted.

before: until the day of the crucifixion
after: until the days of the crucifixion
reason: The correction from day to days here is required because the former is inconsistent with the ensuing narrative.

before: a certain beggar named Lazarus, who laid at
after: a certain beggar named Lazarus, who was laid at
reason: The authors of Part IV generally follow the text of the American Standard Version of 1901.

before: so-called Messianic prophesies
after: so-called Messianic prophecies
reason: Prophesy is the spelling used for the verb, whereas prophecy is the correct spelling for the noun

before: If any one asks you
after: If anyone asks you
reason: Anyone is correct if anybody could be substituted.

before: his associates whom he feared might be led away
after: his associates who he feared might be led away
reason: The pronoun is the subject of the verb phrase might be led away, not the object of feared; therefore who is the correct form.

before: some of the twelve whom he knew were armed
after: some of the twelve who he knew were armed
reason: The pronoun is the subject of the verb were armed, not the object of knew nor of were armed; therefore who is the correct form.

before: the size of a tencent piece
after: the size of a ten-cent piece
reason: The hyphenated word ten-cent is the standard form and is specified by Chicago Manual of Style.

before: except he who received
after: except him who received
reason: The pronoun is the object of the preposition except; therefore him is correct.

before: willing to forego the great advantage
after: willing to forgo the great advantage
reason: The corrected spelling of forgo is etymologically preferable.

before: shortly after 10 o’clock
after: shortly after ten o’clock
reason: The spelled-out form for time is clearly supported in Chicago Manual of Style.

before: still others whom you think love the truth
after: still others who you think love the truth
reason: The pronoun is the subject of love, not the object of think; therefore who is the correct form.

before: he said to the twelve
after: he said to the eleven
reason: There were only eleven apostles with Jesus at this point in the narrative.

before: you shall all some time sup with me
after: you shall all sometime sup with me
reason: The closed form is correct as the reference is to an indefinite point in time.

before: even when faint-hearted believers turn
after: even when fainthearted believers turn
reason: This adverbial variant is particularly strange in hyphenated form, so the closed form was decided upon.

before: to which you shall some time ascend
after: to which you shall sometime ascend
reason: The closed form is correct as the reference is to an indefinite point in time.

before: informal charges of law-breaking
after: informal charges of lawbreaking
reason: Of the five occurrences of lawbreaker and lawbreaking in the text, three are closed and two are hyphenated. There is no differential in meaning, so text standardization in the closed form was decided upon.

before: with this law-breaker
after: with this lawbreaker
reason: Of the five occurrences of lawbreaker and lawbreaking in the text, three are closed and two are hyphenated. There is no differential in meaning, so text standardization in the closed form was decided upon.

before: Sidon, Schechem, Hebron
after: Sidon, Shechem, Hebron
reason: Shechem is the standard transliteration of the name.

before: between man and his Maker on this world
after: between man and his Maker, on this world
reason: The addition of the comma after Maker properly sets off the parenthetical phrase that follows.

before: sandstorms from the Arabian desert
after: sandstorms from the Arabian Desert
reason: The formatting of geographic names is covered by Chicago Manual of Style; the correct form is Arabian Desert.

before: the evildoing of his ancestors
after: the evil-doing of his ancestors
reason: There has been a clear preference for the hyphenated form since the seventeenth century.

before: the tendency toward evildoing
after: the tendency toward evil-doing
reason: There has been a clear preference for the hyphenated form since the seventeenth century.

before: suggested that any one claiming to have seen him
after: suggested that anyone claiming to have seen him
reason: Anyone is correct if anybody could be substituted.

before: the far-away ascetics teach reverence
after: the faraway ascetics teach reverence
reason: Except for this single instance, The Urantia Book uses the closed form.

before: all their new concept of God
after: all their new concepts of God
reason: The inclusion of all here requires the plural concepts.

before: Poutaenus taught Clement and then went on
after: Pantaenus taught Clement and then went on
reason: Pantaenus is the correct spelling.

before: the spirit of the Father is in his Son’s sons
after: the spirit of the Father is in his Sons’ sons
reason: Sons’ is correct in light of the prior sentence which provides the context: this life of the Father is in his Sons.
